slides.title: Matrices and incubation conditions
bullets: Microsomal CLint: human and rat liver microsomes, 0.5 mg/mL protein, 1 µM
Hepatocyte depletion CLint: human and rat cryopreserved cells, 0.5 × 10^6 cells/mL, 1 µM
Keep species and normalization separate throughout the assay worksheet
slides.notes: Protein-normalized and cell-normalized clearances cannot be compared as interchangeable units. No scaled hepatic clearance calculation is included.
slides.footer: Merrivoss Bioanalysis Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Matrix acceptance before ranking
bullets: Helen Marchwood: review matrix acceptance against the assay worksheet
Javier Quintana: review parent-analyte response, blank matrix and carryover
Inspect nonmetabolic loss and the evaluable depletion interval before assigning a biological difference
slides.notes: Acceptance belongs to the incubation and analytical sequence. A favorable clearance estimate is not itself evidence that the matrix was acceptable.
slides.footer: Merrivoss Bioanalysis Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Analytical limits and fit assumptions
bullets: Fit the log-linear parent depletion interval; do not extend a slope through terminal signal below quantitation
A half-life beyond the incubation window is a bound, not a precise turnover estimate
Parent disappearance alone does not identify an enzyme or metabolite
slides.notes: No compound-specific quantitation limits are supplied here. Consult the analyte card before using a marginal slope for selection.

slides.title: Exposure gate: paired-system interpretation
bullets: Hepatocyte turnover revealed a clearance route missing from the microsomal screen, changing Kelbravik's shortlist.
Do not carry the microsomal preference forward without the intact-cell assessment
These incubations do not establish oral exposure
slides.notes: The decision is the recorded project outcome. No individual shortlist or new progression threshold is supplied. Cross-system disagreement does not identify its mechanism.
